whatItDoes: Checks the contrast ratio between a foreground text color and a background color, then reports whether the pair passes WCAG 2.2 AA or AAA requirements for normal text, large text, and UI components. Includes relative luminance calculation, a live preview panel, and a palette of common color pairs.
whyItExists: Low-contrast text is one of the most common accessibility failures on the web and a leading cause of WCAG violations. Designers and developers need a fast, accurate way to verify that color choices meet the contrast thresholds required by WCAG 2.2 and other accessibility standards.
whoShouldUse: UI and UX designers validating color systems, front-end developers building accessible interfaces, accessibility specialists auditing sites, and content teams ensuring readable text on any background.
useCases: Verify text color contrast against a background before publishing a design
Audit an existing color palette to find AA or AAA compliant pairs
Check large-text and UI-component thresholds separately per WCAG 2.2
Pick a compliant text shade by previewing the ratio against your brand background
instructions: Pick a foreground text color using the color inputs or HEX text boxes
Pick a background color the same way
Read the computed contrast ratio and the AA/AAA pass status
Use the live preview to see how the colors look together
Toggle the preview for normal text, large text, and UI components
Use the palette list to check multiple common color pairs at once
examples: #ffffff on #000000 → ratio 21.00:1 → AAA Pass for all text sizes
#767676 on #ffffff → ratio 4.54:1 → AA Pass for normal text, AAA Fail
#ff6600 on #ffffff → ratio 2.85:1 → AA Fail for normal text, AA Pass for large text
#1a73e8 on #ffffff → ratio 4.56:1 → AA Pass for normal text
bestPractices: Design for AA as a minimum; use AAA only where there is no long-form text
Test at 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text (18pt/14pt bold)
Check your palette in both light and dark modes, since ratios differ
Avoid relying on color alone — pair contrast with non-color cues
commonMistakes: Testing only one text size when the page uses many sizes
Assuming a brand color is accessible without measuring its ratio
Ignoring the background of hover and focus states
Using 4.5:1 for large text and wrongly rejecting accessible colors
Not checking the contrast of placeholder text and disabled states
faq: What contrast ratio does WCAG 2.2 require? — 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text (18pt or 14pt bold), and 3:1 for UI components.
What is relative luminance? — A normalized measure of a color's brightness, defined by the WCAG formula using linearized RGB channels.
Does this tool store my colors? — No, all calculation happens locally in your browser. Nothing is uploaded.
Why does my colored text fail even though it looks readable? — Perceptual readability and the WCAG mathematical ratio are different; the ratio is the standard that auditors check.
What is the difference between AA and AAA? — AAA requires a higher ratio (7:1 for normal text, 4.5:1 for large text) than AA.
features: WCAG 2.2 AA and AAA pass/fail checks
Normal text, large text, and UI component thresholds
HEX, RGB, and HSL color input
Quick-check palette of common color pairs
